messages.subject: Spatial Dependence in Custom Model
parts:
Hi, 
I need your help to configure the program PRESENCE for Spatial dependence customs model. 

Subject:
In nature, water vole, muskrat and coypu seem to coexist at large scale in Normandy. Even if this hypothesis was studied at large scale of this study, we have also pursued to investigate a potential spatial segregation between species to explain their coexistence within a habitat. For the local scale, within the 98 sites prospected, those with more than 2 detections of water vole and 2 detections of muskrat and/or coypu were selected (N=16). Each original transect was subdivised into 10 subunits (hereafter “segments”) of 20m that constituted the adjacent spatial replicates. Each segment was sampled only once (between June 15th and 30th) during 10 minutes, by the same observer in order to detect presence signs of water vole, muskrat and coypu (faeces). In each segment, we also characterized the type (mesophilic or hygrophile plant, woody vegetation) and the height (>30cm) of riparian vegetation located between 0-50cm and 50cm-2m from the riverside. Surveys were always carried out in periods without precipitation, both during the sampling period and at least the previous four days, to avoid eventual disappearance of presence signs.

The objective it's to identify the impact of every invasive species on the presence of arvicola sapidus. Coypu and muskrat have a home range more important than segment, the model with twho species isn't adaptive. I'm interested how affect every species on arvicola. I thought used data on invasive species as covariates. 
Finally, i would like to compare the probability of presence of arvicola according all covariates (presence of coypu, presence of muskrat and others environmental parameters), without forget dependence spatial replicate. 

On the website of program PRESENCE, there is "Spatial dependence in customs model", but i don't know how applicate this model on the program and configurate the matrix.

Can you help me??

Emilie
